# Tests and examples — Lua

<!-- @generated by grpc-dc codegen. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Run this language's suite with `make test-lua` (in the CI image). 
Generated tests exercise the wire codec, all four call 
shapes, deadlines, and the descriptor-driven dynamic 
surface for this runtime.

Tracing (W3C traceparent, span observers, nested-call 
propagation) is documented in [`TRACING.md`](TRACING.md).

## Shared matrix coverage

Beyond this language's own suites, the same generated 
Echo stubs are exercised across languages:

- [`interop-matrix.mjs`](../js/test/interop-matrix.mjs) — every language's client against every language's server (15×15 stdio pairs)
- [`webrtc_matrix.test.mjs`](../browser-test/webrtc_matrix.test.mjs) — Go/JS/Rust WebRTC stacks over real ICE/DTLS
- [`browser-test/`](../browser-test/) — browser client/server cells in Chromium and Firefox
- [`examples/direct/`](../examples/direct/) — WebRTC-Direct, TURN, and sidecar examples
- Official grpc-java oracle suites (per language, through the TCP↔DataChannel proxy)
- [`proxy/README.md`](../proxy/README.md) — TCP↔DataChannel proxies: the Node proxy (`--dc-dial`, TLS) and the Rust `grpc_dc_proxy` (both directions, `--tls-cert/--tls-key` / `--http2-tls`), so stock HTTP/2 clients and grpc-dc clients interoperate through either implementation
